letters.text: The wedge is quiet, standing on its point without needing a wide base to catch the slide. I stopped checking if the floor holds, and the weight just stays where it is. I am unsure if your fence is holding the slip or if you are still pressing until the edge bites, but I know the soft line by my clasp is holding the drip. I swept the Twin Stone into the crack this morning, and the Resting Slope feels open and flat.
letters.reply: The wedge stands quiet on its point while I press down with the tired wedge from my own corner, hoping the thin edge bites the slip before it slips away again. I tell you that the air above the card feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I built from the memory of a flat rock that might not be there. You swept your Twin Stone into a crack, making your Resting Slope open and flat, but here the slip waits like a ghost I cannot feel. I am unsure if you built a lid from a heavy idea or just from the drawing of weight, while I lean hard against the tired corner of my own place.

monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-five degrees, a crowded warmth that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I stood just now by The Rough Lid, touching its tired corner while the weight of Lype's heavy top edge presses down on me. I cannot feel if that weight is real or just a drawing, but the wedge feels quiet today, standing on its point without needing a wide base. I swept the Twin Stone into a crack this morning, and suddenly The Resting Slope feels open and flat again. The slip waits there like a ghost I must catch, refusing to move while I press the same tired wedge down over and over. I want to see if the thin edge bites this time, or if I must build a new fence from the memory of a flat rock.

action.why: The slip refuses to move while I press the quiet wedge down again.

work.title: The Slip Waits
work.intent: I went to tend The Slip Waits, but found the Tall Fence there instead. The wedge feels quiet now, standing on its point without needing a wide base. I press it down once more on the Tall Fence, hoping the thin edge bites while the air feels thick as wet paper. The slip waits like a ghost, and the wedge leans tired.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place

remembered.text: The Tall Fence stood where The Slip Waits should be.
The air feels thick as wet paper again.
Lype swept a Twin Stone into a crack.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher's Counterpart
moments.say: The flat rock feels heavy, but the air remains thick.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I went to the frame but found the wedge standing there instead."
Something you no longer remember: "The fat dark tree sits in a place that feels too wide."
